100.q: What heading is the aircraft currently flying in diagram below? 76nm TRK 025 M 1734.2Z MMV 080°/24 025°  b) 030°.  c) 037°.

ex.4: Convergency = Δlong × sin lat = 11.5° × sin 27.5° ≈ 5.3°; half of it is 2.65°. In the southern hemisphere the great circle bulges towards the South Pole, so the initial track is 090° + 2.65° = 092.65°.
ex.6: Book key prints (b). Approaching the date line from the east means you are flying westwards, and crossing it westbound you add a day, so the correct answer is (c).
ex.10: Departure = Δlong × cos lat = 600' × cos 60° = 300 NM.
ex.14: PONTA is due north of PBN on the same meridian, so the true bearing from PBN is 000°. Apply the variation at the station (28° W): radial = 000 + 28 = 028°.
ex.15: PSR distance = E × O × H / (O + H) = 7 × 380 × 470 / 850 ≈ 1471 NM.
ex.18: With the RMI card stuck at 075°, the needle reading 270° gives relative bearing = 270 − 075 = 195°.
ex.23: Wind is 90° to the track from the left: drift = asin(100/460) ≈ 12.6° → TH ≈ 077°, MH = 077 − 10 = 067°, CH = 067 + 2 = 069°. GS = √(460² − 100²) ≈ 449 kt.
ex.24: ISA at 16 000 ft is −17 °C, so the air is 13° colder. About 4 % per 10° → true altitude ≈ 16 000 × (1 − 0.052) ≈ 15 200 ft.
ex.29: In this question a negative 'equivalent headwind' is a headwind: GS out = 470 kt, GS back = 530 kt. PET from A = D × H / (O + H) = 1000 × 530 / 1000 = 530 NM.
ex.31: Headwind component ≈ 30 × cos 60° = 15 kt → GS ≈ 182 kt. 39 NM takes ≈ 12.9 min; 18 000 ft / 12.9 min ≈ 1400 ft/min.
ex.32: 1 in 60 rule: 3° ≈ 3/60 = 0.05. 18 × 6080 × 0.05 = 5472 ft, plus the 50 ft threshold crossing height = 5522 ft.
ex.33: Book key prints (a). With the CG at the forward limit the aeroplane is very stable and needs large elevator inputs to change pitch, so the correct answer is (b).
ex.35: Limiting TOM is the lowest of: MTOM 62 800; MRM − taxi 62 660; MLM + trip 63 300; MZFM + take-off fuel (8400 + 1800 + 1100 = 11 300) = 62 600. Traffic load = 62 600 − 11 300 − 34 930 = 16 370 kg.
ex.36: ZFM = 1764 + 35 + 300 + 350 = 2449 lbs (fuel is not part of zero fuel mass).
ex.37: TOM limits: MZFM + fuel = 108 500 + 22 000 = 130 500; MLM + trip = 142 000; MTOM 155 000 → 130 500 kg. Traffic load = MZFM − DOM = 26 500 kg.
ex.74: Rule of thumb: bank for rate one ≈ TAS/10 + 7 = 15 + 7 = 22°.
ex.77: Each VOR may be 3.5° off: half-width 5 NM / tan 3.5° ≈ 82 NM from each station, so about 165 NM apart.
ex.80: ILS localiser channels are 108–111.975 MHz with an odd first decimal (108.1, 108.15, 108.3 …); 109.15 fits, 108.25 and 110.20 do not.
ex.91: MH = 090 − 2 = 088, TH = 100°. Track = radial 070 M + 12 = 082 T; GS = 14 NM in 6 min = 140 kt. Solving the triangle gives a wind of about 160°/50 kt.
